title: Space bound for compiled decisions
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $M_0,M_1$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, and let $A_0,A_1$ be languages of Boolean words. Suppose that each $M_j$ decides $A_j$ with space bound $s_j$. For Boolean words $x,v,w$, assume that for every $i\le |v|$, the encoding of $x$ paired with the binary expansion of $i$ belongs to $A_0$ if and only if $i<|v|$, and for every $i<|v|$, that encoding belongs to $A_1$ if and only if the $i$th bit of $v$, taken to be false when absent, is true. Suppose that $M$ on input $v$ halts after $t$ steps with output $w$, and that $B$ is a natural number such that, for both $j=0,1$ and every $i\le |v|$, the maximum of $s_j$ at the length of the encoded input and $1$ is at most $B$. Then the compiled machine constructed from $M$ and the two deciders halts on input $x$ with output $w$ at some time $T$, and its space usage by time $T$ is at most $M.k\bigl(2\,\mathrm{space}_M(v,t)+1\bigr)+\bigl(|\mathrm{bits}(|v|+1)|+2\bigr)+2K(2B+1)$, where $K$ is the maximum number of work tapes of $M_0$ and $M_1$.
